[Buyer]: I’m really frustrated at this point and not sure what else to do.

I ordered this custom office chair because I work from home full-time and needed something supportive. The listing promised “premium upholstery with no visible defects” and “precision-aligned armrests and back support.” I paid almost $400, which is a lot of money for me.

The chair showed up almost a week later than the estimated delivery window. I tried to be understanding about that, but when I unpacked it, I noticed a few issues right away:
- The right armrest is visibly crooked compared to the left. You can see it tilting inward in the photos I attached.
- There are loose threads and fraying on the seat fabric along one seam.
- When I sit in it for more than 20–30 minutes, the back feels uneven, like it’s pushing more on one side.

I reached out to the seller first. They told me this is “within normal manufacturing tolerances” and basically implied I’m being too picky. They offered a small partial refund (which wouldn’t even cover having someone try to fix it locally) or just sending a replacement armrest, but that doesn’t solve the fabric issue or the weird support.

I’m honestly feeling pretty let down and a bit taken advantage of. This was supposed to help my back, and now I feel stuck with something that doesn’t match what was advertised. I’ve tried to explain that to the seller, but I don’t feel heard at all.

What I would like is either a full refund with them covering return shipping, or at least a proper replacement that doesn’t have these defects. I’m open to suggestions, but I need an outcome that actually feels fair, not just a token credit.

Can someone here please look at this seriously and tell me what my options are? I just want to feel like this is being handled fairly.

[Seller]: Hello,

I understand the buyer is disappointed, but from our perspective the chair is within acceptable quality standards. We hand-assemble these, and slight variation in armrest angle (a few millimeters) is normal and does not affect function. The photos they sent show what, in our experience, is typical alignment.

Regarding the fabric, the “fraying” appears to be loose threads from the manufacturing process, which can usually be trimmed off without any issue. We do not see evidence of a tear or structural defect in the upholstery.

We have already offered a goodwill gesture: either a $40 partial refund or sending a replacement right armrest at no cost. A full refund including return shipping on a custom item like this would be a significant loss to us and is not something we can generally do unless there is a clear, major defect.

We are a small business, and if we start giving full refunds every time someone dislikes a minor imperfection, we won’t survive. We are trying to be reasonable and stay within what we can afford.
